title: Stratified perfect description of the integral completed category
statement: Use the coefficient conventions of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] and schemes of [def-pc-scheme]. Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and let $T$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Here noetherian means that $T$ has a finite affine cover by spectra of noetherian rings, finite-dimensional means a finite bound on the lengths of strict chains of irreducible closed subsets, and invertible means that $\ell\cdot1$ is a unit in each local ring. Put $A_T=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_T$ as in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the following conditions are equivalent: (i) $K$ belongs to [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], including its compatible etale-origin witnesses; (ii) there is a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification] such that on each stratum $K$ is pro-etale locally isomorphic to $A_T\otimes_A^L P$ for a perfect $A$-complex $P$, meaning a bounded complex of finite projective $A$-modules; (iii) $K$ is bounded and every cohomology sheaf, after a finite stratification, is pro-etale locally $A_T\otimes_A N$ for a finitely presented $A$-module $N$. These conditions also describe exactly the category of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] whenever that notation is used over such a $T$, with the same completed ring sheaf and reduction functors. This full subcategory is closed under shifts, cones, standard truncations and cohomology sheaves placed in degree zero.

source.place: Definition 6.5.1; Proposition 6.6.11; Proposition 6.8.11(1),(3). Adapted to the explicitly retained compatible etale-origin witnesses and uniform reduction bounds of the DAG; those clauses must be verified, not identified by notation.

proof.text: Fix the completed coefficient convention throughout. The completed-constant reduction lemma gives flatness of $A_T$ over the constant $A$-sheaf and $A_T\otimes_A^L A/\varpi^n\simeq(A/\varpi^n)_T$. For a stratum immersion $i:S\to T$, inverse image is exact and preserves limits, hence $i^{-1}A_T=A_S$; for a site object $U\to S$, slice restriction has the same property by the localization description. Since the coefficient map $c$ is an isomorphism, module pullback $u^*=u^{-1}(-)\otimes_{u^{-1}A_T,c}A_S$ is exact, so it equals its left derived functor, and the derived tensor-pullback lemma gives $u^{-1}(K\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T)\simeq u^{-1}K\otimes^L_{A_S}(P_n)_S$, naturally in the quotient maps. In particular these restrictions preserve finite reductions and their normalization maps. To check completeness, use the quotient-tower completion unit furnished by the constant-completion equivalence. Exact countable products compute derived products termwise, and the strict-tower Roos triangle computes its derived limit. Exact restriction preserving products therefore preserves this unit and its cone. The finite-stratum detection lemma, followed by covering detection of zero sheaves, shows that the cone vanishes on $T$ if and only if it vanishes on all chosen stratum covers. Thus intrinsic completeness restricts to strata and covers and is detected on a finite stratification. This argument uses the actual coefficient isomorphism for immersions and slices, not scalar extension along an arbitrary scheme morphism.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.8(1),(2); Proposition 6.6.11, restriction and completeness devissage; explicit Roos-cone argument

proof.text: For a bounded finite-projective $A$-complex $P$, its completed constant realization is $A_U\otimes_A P$ termwise. Its finite reductions are the constant complexes $P\otimes_A A/\varpi^n$ by the completed-constant reduction lemma. In each degree the finite-projective module is a summand of $A^r$; the transition maps on the corresponding constant sheaves are sectionwise surjective by the constant-module section lemma. On products of this tower, $1-s$ is sectionwise surjective: given $(y_n)$, choose $x_1$ and recursively lift $x_n-y_n$ to $x_{n+1}$, so $x_n-q(x_{n+1})=y_n$. Its kernel is the inverse limit. The limit of a finite-projective summand is the same summand of $A_U^r$. The Roos triangle therefore identifies the quotient completion unit with an isomorphism onto the original realized complex. Such a complex is intrinsically complete. A finite stratification with perfect local models has globally bounded cohomology and globally bounded reductions: the finite Noetherian affine cover of $T$ makes its underlying space Noetherian (a descending closed chain stabilizes on each affine member). Every subset of that space is quasi-compact, hence so is each stratum. Thus the covering axiom of the pro-etale site allows finitely many quasi-compact pieces of the trivializing cover to cover it; take the smallest and largest term degrees of their finitely many models. The finite-stratum detection lemma detects vanishing outside these bounds. Completeness also follows from step 1.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, reverse implication; completed perfect constants and finite bounds

proof.text: First verify the coefficient completeness needed below. The coefficient ring is adically complete: for a compatible family in $A/\varpi^n$, choose representatives $x_n\in A$. Compatibility gives $x_{n+1}-x_n\in\varpi^nA$, so $|x_m-x_n|_E\leq|\varpi|_E^n$ for $m\geq n$. Completeness of $E$ gives a limit $x$ in its closed unit ball $A$; each closed ball $x_n+\varpi^nA$ contains that limit. Thus $x$ has the prescribed residues, and $\bigcap_n\varpi^nA=0$ gives uniqueness. This verifies the extra adic-completeness hypothesis of the lifting lemma.

source.place: Section 6.5, complete coefficient hypothesis; elementary Cauchy-sequence verification for the chosen valuation ring

proof.text: Assume (i). The uniform tower definition gives local complexes in a fixed term interval $[d_0,d_1]$, and every cohomology sheaf of $K_1$ is finite lisse on its finite stratification. Uniform boundedness of the derived reductions requires a separate check: for every $n\geq1$, over the DVR $A$, $[A\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}A]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$ resolves $A/\varpi^n$. Flatness and finite reduction in the completed-constant reduction lemma therefore give the flat resolution $[A_T\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}A_T]$ of $(A/\varpi^n)_T$. Tensoring a local complex from the uniform tower definition with this resolution has terms only in $[d_0-1,d_1]$. Its quasi-isomorphism with $K_n$ on the chosen covers, and the finite-stratum detection of step 1, give that same global cohomological interval independently of $n$.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, forward implication; local ingredient Lemma 6.6.8 and Stacks Tag 09C6

proof.text: Continue with (i) and the reduction bounds of step 4. In particular $K_1$ is bounded with intrinsically constructible cohomology: on the strata and covers of the uniform tower its cohomology sheaves are finite lisse. Every locally closed subset of $T$ is constructible: the underlying space of $T$ is Noetherian (step 2), and in a Noetherian space every finite union of locally closed subsets is constructible by the definition of constructible subsets. So the strata of every finite stratification used here satisfy the constructibility clause of intrinsic pro-etale constructibility. Finite-ring derived origin gives a bounded constructible etale complex $L_1$ with $\nu_T^*L_1\simeq K_1$; one may use the existing compatible witness, since bounded-below full faithfulness identifies it with this origin. By the definition of etale constructibility choose a finite stratification on which all the finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves of $L_1$ are finite locally constant. A common refinement is obtained by intersecting the finitely many locally closed partitions and using their fibre-product immersions. Comparison-pullback identifies its restriction to every new stratum with the corresponding restriction of $K_1$. Apply finite-ring derived local constancy on each stratum to $L_1$. Since $A/\varpi$ is a field, its bounded finite-module constant models are perfect: split cycles and boundaries as vector spaces to replace the complex by its finitely many finite-dimensional cohomology spaces in their degrees. Step 1 makes $K$ intrinsically complete on every stratum. By step 3 the coefficient ring is adically complete. The residue-lisse perfect-lifting lemma now gives pro-etale locally a perfect $A$-complex on each stratum. This proves (ii). No claim is made that a general finite-ring bounded complex is perfect; the residue field is essential here.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, forward implication; local ingredient Lemma 6.6.8 and Stacks Tag 09C6

proof.text: Assume (ii). Steps 1 and 2 give intrinsic completeness and a common cohomological interval for all reductions $K_n$. Their restrictions to the given strata are constant perfect $(A/\varpi^n)$-complexes locally, so every finite-level cohomology sheaf is finite lisse there, hence intrinsically constructible, the strata being constructible as in step 5. The quotient tower has the strict realization and normalization cocycle of the coefficient-datum definition. Normalized constructible local effectivity supplies exactly the common local models required by the uniform tower definition. Finite-ring derived origin supplies $L_n\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A/\varpi^n)$ and $\alpha_n:\nu_T^*L_n\simeq K_n$. Pullback commutes with coefficient tensor, so the source $L_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A/\varpi^{n+1}}A/\varpi^n$ pulls back to $K_n$. Exact finite-level comparison reflects zero cohomology sheaves, by its sheaf unit; therefore this source is bounded before bounded-below full faithfulness is applied. Lift $\alpha_n^{-1}\rho_n(\alpha_{n+1}\otimes^L A/\varpi^n)$ uniquely by full faithfulness to $\beta_n$. Its inverse also lifts, so $\beta_n$ is an isomorphism. Faithfulness turns the quotient-cocycle equalities after pullback into equalities of the lifted maps. These are compatible etale-origin witnesses as required, not unrelated levelwise origins. All conditions of (i) hold.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, reverse implication; explicit verification of the DAG uniform models and compatible witnesses

proof.text: Assume (ii). On a perfect local model $P$, flatness over the constant $A$-sheaf identifies $\mathcal H^q(A_U\otimes_A P)$ with $A_U\otimes_A H^q(P)$. The kernels of the differentials in the finite-projective terms of $P$ are finitely generated by Noetherian submodule finiteness, and their quotient cohomology modules are finitely generated. They are finitely presented over $A$ by the Noetherian finite-presentation lemma. Step 2 supplies the global finite cohomological bound. These descriptions on the same strata are precisely (iii).

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), constructible complexes have constructible cohomology; Proposition 6.6.11 local models

proof.text: Let $C$ be any cohomology sheaf allowed by (iii). On a stratum cover it is $A_U\otimes_A N$ with $N$ finitely presented. Choose a surjection $A^r\to N$. Its kernel is finitely generated by Noetherian submodule finiteness and torsion-free as a submodule of $A^r$. The DVR torsion-free module lemma makes it finite free. Thus $0\to A^s\to A^r\to N\to0$ gives a perfect $A$-complex in degrees $[-1,0]$. Flatness of $A_U$ over the constant $A$-sheaf realizes this resolution with cohomology exactly $C$ in degree zero. This proves (ii) for $C[0]$, with the same two term bounds on all strata and covers; step 6 proves (i) for $C[0]$. This is a resolution argument, not an additional node restating the degree-zero clause.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), finitely presented integral modules have finite projective resolutions

proof.text: Assume (iii), with $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. Step 8 puts each $\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]$ in (i). Start with $\tau^{\leq a-1}K=0$. For $q=a,\ldots,b$, the standard truncation triangle has vertices $\tau^{\leq q-1}K$, $\tau^{\leq q}K$, and $\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]$. Inductively the outer vertices belong to (i), and the uniform-complete triangulated lemma puts the middle vertex in (i). At $q=b$ the middle vertex is $K$. This proves (iii) implies (i), completing all three equivalences. The induction is finite; it does not commute truncation with finite coefficient reduction.

For the detailed integral notation, use it only under its own coefficient hypotheses and with the same completed ring and reduction functors. The finite-torsion and intrinsic pro-etale constructibility definitions both ask for a finite partition into constructible locally closed strata on which the sheaf is pro-etale locally constant with finite stalks; locally closed strata of $T$ are constructible as in step 5. Membership in (i) implies levelwise finite-torsion constructibility and the uniform interval, hence the reduction conditions of the detailed definition. Intrinsic completeness is the quotient completion condition by the constant-completion equivalence, and its Roos triangle supplies the completeness condition of the detailed definition. Conversely a detailed object has intrinsically constructible finite-level cohomology and the stipulated common interval. Its completeness Roos triangle identifies its underlying object with the quotient derived limit. The latter is the Koszul completion object and is intrinsically complete by the completion-reflector lemma; completeness is invariant under isomorphism. This argument only needs the object identification and does not assert uniqueness of a lift of its projection maps. Normalized constructible local effectivity gives the required uniform tower models, and the full-faithfulness lifting argument in step 6 gives compatible etale witnesses. Thus it belongs to (i). No equality between the constant and completed ambient module categories is used.

source.place: Definition 6.5.1 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); comparison with the two explicitly defined DAG integral categories

proof.text: The uniform-complete triangulated lemma gives closure under shifts and cones of every ambient morphism. By (iii), $\tau^{\leq m}K$, $\tau^{\geq m}K$ and $\mathcal H^q(K)[0]$ are bounded and have the same permitted cohomology sheaves, with some degrees replaced by zero. The standard t-structure gives these cohomology descriptions. The implication (iii) implies (i) already proved puts all these objects in the category. This proves unrestricted standard truncation closure, without the Tor-compatibility assumption of the distinct levelwise-truncation construction.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), stability under standard truncations and cohomology
